summary: Bundled skill scripts perform routine network calls; no installer-side attack observed
details: Package ships a collection of 'skills' containing helper scripts. Static keyword co-occurrence fired on: a Python scraper base (bundled-skills/junta-leiloeiros/scripts/scraper/base_scraper.py) making GET/POST/ping calls consistent with a web-scraping helper; a local API server script (serve_api.py) with GET routes; a benchmark runner (bundled-skills/loki-mode/benchmarks/run-benchmarks.sh) referencing curl and an 'install' string; an rclone helper (bundled-skills/rclone-cli/scripts/install.sh) that fetches from rclone.org (the official rclone project domain); and a YouTube-notetaker verify script issuing curl GETs. None of these are invoked from npm lifecycle hooks or top-level module code — they are opt-in helper scripts a user would explicitly run. No hardcoded attacker C2, no credential/env-var scraping, no filesystem secret enumeration, no obfuscation, no fetch-and-execute of remote code, and the one third-party fetch targets the tool's own official domain (rclone.org).

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
